title: Add structured data with JSON-LD
when: The user wants rich search results for a business, product, article, event, recipe or FAQ page.
inputs: the facts shown on the page
prompt:
Goal: Valid JSON-LD that uses the right schema.org type and repeats only facts visible on the page.
Steps:
1. Pick the type from the page purpose: LocalBusiness (or a subtype such as Bakery), Product with Offer, Article, Event, Recipe, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList.
2. Add one <script type="application/ld+json"> in the head with "@context": "https://schema.org" and "@type".
3. Fill required and recommended properties with the real values: name, address as PostalAddress, telephone, openingHoursSpecification, price and priceCurrency.
4. Use ISO formats: dates as 2026-05-01T19:00, durations as PT30M, currency codes such as BRL or EUR.
5. Give every page at least a WebPage or BreadcrumbList block so each page carries valid data.
6. Validate by parsing the JSON and checking every value appears in the visible content.
Quality bar:
- The JSON parses.
- Values match the visible text exactly.
- One block per entity, linked with @id when related.
Pitfalls:
- Trailing commas or comments, which break JSON.
- Marking up reviews or ratings that are not on the page.
- Wrong nesting such as price outside offers.
Verify:
- [ ] Each page has a JSON-LD block that parses.
- [ ] The @type fits the content.
- [ ] Dates and prices use ISO formats.
- [ ] No invented facts.
Output: JSON-LD blocks added to the head of each page.

examples.input: add schema to my event page
examples.output: Event with name, startDate 2026-11-20T20:00, location Place with address, offers with price 40 BRL
